convoLines.text: "What scares you most about what's happening? The real answer."
They go quiet. "Yeah. Me too. The randomness would almost be kinder."
"...What's that supposed to mean?" Their voice goes careful.
"Still on what scares you most."
"Yes. Absolutely. I've been hoping you'd ask." (A little too quickly.)
"...I need to go be quiet for a while."
They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"Teach me something. Anything you know that I don't."
"Okay." Something shutters, just slightly.
"Still on teaching them something."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Roman is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
You show them Serviceberry — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"I keep turning over the last thing Roman said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
"Nobody says Roman's name right yet. We will. Give it a few days."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
Something eases in their shoulders. They're really talking to you now.
"Right. Go on, then."
"This was good." They mean it.
"You said the scary part is this might be on purpose. That someone's watching. Believing it more or less these days?"
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
Something crosses their face — quick, then gone. The practiced expression clicks back into place.

A wall comes down, then — surprisingly — a door opens behind it. "I'm not from Denver. I'm from Budapest, Hungary. I keep my head down. Old habit. It kept me alive before; it keeps me alive now." Quiet. Real.
Zoltan looks at you, level. "I told you the truth. You can keep poking it, but it's told."
"That again?" Zoltan sighs. "I confessed that already. I'm not confessing it twice for dramatic effect."
"You're really going to make me say it again?" Zoltan rubs their face. "Fine — but it's the same truth as last time."
"We went over this," Zoltan says, a little tired. "I already told you the truth about that."
"Still on that personal stuff."
You show them Serviceberry — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Can we talk?" Ava sits down near you. "Just... talk. Like people used to."
"What's the most useful thing you've learned since we got here?"
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
The ease drains out of it, a little.
"Still on the most useful thing you've learned."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up, friend?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "Roman owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
You show them White Oak Acorns — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"When's the last time you really laughed? Just... be straight with me."
"It feels wrong because it matters. The wrong-feeling things are usually the important ones. That is all."
"Still on the last time you laughed."
"What do you make of all this? Really."
"Bleak. Probably true. I keep looking for the part where it's not."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Good question." "Last time things were different. They always are." "They took me. The Lottery — up there, on the screens, in front of everyone. I'm still turning it over."
"That's the whole of it. Sorry."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Sure. I'll be around."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"Can I tell you something? I've been sneaking out at night. I'm ashamed and I can't stop."
"Help me haul something back? Too much for one."
It's quiet at the cache spot. Zoltan doesn't say much. Sometimes that's the whole point.
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on their secret."
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"...Anyway. What did you want to ask?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "You saw it too, right? The Lottery. Tell me I didn't imagine the lights."
"Ask me tomorrow. Everything changes by tomorrow."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Can we talk?" Miguel sits down near you. "Just... talk. Like people used to."
"Help me haul something back? Too much for one."
Miguel shows you where they go to think. "Don't tell the others. Everyone needs one place."
"Got a read on anyone here yet? Who should I be watching?"
"Okay." Something shutters, just slightly.
"Still on your read on people here. You'd know about that."
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Can I tell you something? I know who took the extra rations but won't say."
"Walk my trap line with me? Extra hands, extra eyes."
Chloe shows you where they go to think. "Don't tell the others. Everyone needs one place."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Still on their secret."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
You show them Serviceberry — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"Don't tell anyone I told you. What's on your mind?"
"The Iron Pantry. They just... took you. Came back like nothing happened. It wasn't nothing."
"I clean up other people's messes quietly. It passes the time. The time passes anyway."
"And... scene. Good talk."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
